prompt: Candid documentary photo of a real bowl of soto ayam as eaten at a small warung in Java: a wide ceramic bowl of clear, golden-yellow chicken broth (from turmeric) with thin threads of egg yolk, sliced scallion, and fried shallots floating on the surface. Submerged and visible at the top: shredded poached free-range chicken, glass vermicelli noodles (soun), bean sprouts, slices of tomato, a wedge of lime, and a hard-boiled egg cut in half showing the yolk. Two or three krupuk (prawn crackers) standing at the edge of the bowl. A small saucer of sambal on the side, a small dish of steamed white rice. Served on a worn wooden or formica warung table, a glass of warm jasmine tea (teh anget) and other warung bowls softly out of focus behind. Soft natural daylight from the open shopfront, viewed from about 40 degrees above, 35mm lens, moderate depth of field. Everyday unstyled serving, slightly messy edges with broth near the rim, true-to-life colours, realistic textures, a wisp of steam. The broth must be clear golden yellow, not opaque, not milky, not red. No food styling, no microgreens, no fusion garnishes, no studio lighting, no text, no logos, no people, no hands.
